title.narrative: Fundacion Avina: Migrants as Agents for Change

description.narrative:
The main objective of the project Migrants as Agents for Change is to strengthen the social fabric of the migrant population through its institutional strengthening and the advocacy capacity of its grassroots organizations in the northern triangle of Central America. The purpose is that, through their strengthening, they themselves can strengthen their bases, participate in spaces of national and regional strategic incidence, as well as make public policy proposals for the defense of their rights, among them, the right to work.
The overall objective is divided into two general objectives: 1) To strengthen the capacity of migrant led organisations to influence policy, legislation and practice at the local and national level and strengthen human rights for migrants. 2) To design multi-sector mechanisms and establish three-party cooperation to support the socio-economic integration of migrants at local level.

Projektet ”Migranter som förändringsagenter-Stärkande av kapacitet för påverkansarbete och ledarskap hos migrantbaserade organisationer i norra triangeln i Centralameriaka (Guatemala, Honduras och El Salvador) genomförs av Fundación Avina under perioden november 2022 – januari 2024. Huvudsyftet med projektet är att stärka organisationsstrukturer hos migranter och återvändare för ökad kapacitet att delta i nationella och regionala processer, utforma och driva förslag till policys som garanterar migranters rättigheter, bland annat rätten att arbeta. Det övergripande målet är uppdelat i två delmål: 1) Att stärka kapaciteten hos migrantledda organisationer att påverka politik, lagstiftning och praxis på lokal och nationell nivå för att stärka migranters mänskliga rättigheter. 2) Att utforma multisektoriella mekanismer och etablera trepartssamarbete, som sammanför lokala myndigheter, den privata sektorn och det civila samhället, för att stödja socioekonomisk integration av migranter på lokal nivå. Fundación Avina är en latinamerikansk organisation med 25 års erfarenhet av att arbeta med migration, stöd till civilsamhället och ekonomiskt stärkande av migranter i Latinamerika. Fundación Avina kommer att samarbeta med 15 lokala organisationer som arbetar med och för migrationer samt med det regionala nätverket av civilsamhällesorganisationer som arbetar med migrationsfrågor.

The project Migrants as agents for change: Strengthening the advocacy and leadership capacity of migrant based organizations in the Northern Triangle in Central America is implemented by Fundación Avina during the period November 2022 – January 2024. The main objective of the project is to strengthen the social fabric of the migrant population through its institutional strengthening and the advocacy capacity of its grassroots organizations in the northern triangle of Central America. The purpose is that, through their strengthening, they themselves can strengthen their bases, participate in spaces of national and regional strategic incidence, as well as make public policy proposals for the defense of their rights, among them, the right to work. The overall objective is divided into two general objectives: 1) To strengthen the capacity of migrant led organizations to influence policy, legislation and practice at the local and national level and strengthen human rights for migrants. 2) To design multi-sector mechanisms and establish three-party cooperation, bringing together local authorities, private sector and civil society, to support the socio-economic integration of migrants at local level. Fundación Avina is a Latin American organization with 25 years of experience of working with migration, support to civil society and economic empowerment of migrants in Latin America. Fundación Avina will collaborate with 15 local organizations working with and for migrations and with the regional network of civil society organizations working on migration issues.

sector.narrative: Facilitation of orderly, safe, regular and responsible migration and mobility

title.narrative: Grant agreement contribution with Fundación Avina 2022

description.narrative:
2024 Progress and examples of results related to the first objective: Strengthened capacity and advocacy of grass root migrant organisations: Fundación Avina has continued supporting 15 grass root migrant organizations in Guatemala, El Salvador and Honduras to develop and strengthen their organizational structures, planning, networking and advocacy skills and in some cases to obtain legal status, thereby strengthening the sustainability of the organization and the opportunities for future financial support.
A key element of the project has been the strengthening of the organizations' communication and advocacy capabilities. In 2024, the 15 organizations finalized their detailed communication plans with objectives, strategies and dissemination channels. The organizations participated in joint workshops on narrative design and creative writing, which facilitated regional collaboration in transformative communication and narrative generation. An objective of the project's communication strategy is to make visible the work and success stories of grassroots organizations. Interviews with the organizations were collected in video format and a YouTube channel was created to disseminate their stories.
The project has continued to emphasize the inclusion and strengthening of women's leadership. In 2024 37 women participated in a training process for women leaders and several of them have assumed leadership positions within their organizations.
Examples of results from the advocacy work of the participating grass root organizations: A milestone to highlight in 2024 was the active participation of the Committee of Relatives of Missing Migrants of El Progreso (COFAMIPRO) in the advocacy process that resulted in the approval of the first Honduran Protocol for the Search for Missing Migrants on the migratory route. This protocol is a significant advance in the State's response in coordination with civil society and international cooperation. In addition, the process allowed COFAMIPRO to share learning with counterpart organizations in Guatemala and El Salvador.
The advocacy work of the National Commission to Support Returned Migrants with Physical Disabilities (CONAMIREDIS), in Honduras has identified and accompanied migrants with disabilities so that the Secretariat of Social Development grants them identification documents. CONAMIREDIS also participated in the validation of Honduras National Reintegration Plan 2024-2025 addressing the response, protection and assistance needs of migrants returning to the country, contributing to a comprehensive approach to sustainable reintegration.
The Association of Guatemalans United for Our Rights (AGUND) together with other organizations created an Interinstitutional Technical Roundtable to address the situation faced by temporary migrant workers, traveling with work visas to the United States and Canada. The organization also participated in drafting reforms for the registration of recruiters of Guatemalans working abroad.
Progress and examples of results related to the second objective: Multisector mechanisms designed and established for three-party cooperation to support the socioeconomic integration of migrants at local level: Fundación Avina promotes a model of local socioeconomic inclusion that involves various government agencies, the private sector and civil society. The organizational strengthening promoted by the project allowed some of the grassroots organizations to become actively involved in initiatives aimed at promoting alliances with local governments, companies and other actors, in order to promote socioeconomic inclusion initiatives. In 2024, three socio-labor inclusion pilots were implemented in Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador, directly benefiting 458 people with services such as psychosocial care, documentation, training and formal hiring.
An important result is that the municipality of Choloma in Honduras approved the countries first Municipal Public Policy for Attention to Human Mobility. This policy is the result of a collaborative process where government actors, private sector and civil society organizations participated. The perspectives presented by the organizations and private sector representatives are reflected in the guiding principles of the policy, which focus on ensuring the general well being of the mobile population, through access to rights, the full and equitable inclusion of particularly vulnerable groups, such as children, women, older people, indigenous people and people with disabilities. Furthermore, the policy promotes an interinstitutional approach, in which different municipal agencies become involved in caring for migrants. Finally, and very important, the policy enables direct financing and public investment towards the needs of the local agenda and promote strategic alliances between the public and private sectors, civil society, international cooperation and other relevant actors in the process. The policy, with a plan for coordinated actions, is in the process of implementation and a Technical Committee on Migration will monitor and evaluate progress. This policy work can constitute an example to follow for other municipalities in Honduras.
A related progress result is that in the municipality of Olintepeque, in Guatemala, progress was made in the participatory and multi-sectoral development of a municipal policy for socio-labor inclusion of migrants. A proposal was presented to the municipal authorities for approval.
Other results that contribute to the overall objective of the project: In El Salvador, one of the grass root organizations for returned migrants (ASCAPER) has created and is managing a savings and credit cooperative. This has called the attention of many actors due to its innovation in terms of financial inclusion, its potential for replication and sustainability. It is an experience that just begins with the placement of the first credits and for its maturity will require consolidation and alliances that are expected to be consolidated during the remaining project implementation.
The advocacy actions of the Association of Guatemalans United for Our Rights (AGUND) contributed to the formation of an alliance with the organized private sector, academia and international organizations to help establish strategies and actions to improve the conditions of migrant workers. A group was formed to address the issue of Ethical Labor Mobility. This group was invited to be part of the Labor and Labor Mobility Group, made up of government institutions, the ILO and IOM.
In Guatemala and El Salvador new organizations, which were not part of the initial selection of grass root organizations to participate in the project, were identified and have been incorporated into the transversal actions due to their relevance in terms of identifying and strengthening the social fabric that is part of the objectives of the project.
The alliances created and strengthened through the project e.g. made it possible for to 20 people from migrant based organizations in Honduras to receive training in human rights for four months through a collaboration agreement with a well known human rights organization. A Self Care Workshop was also held for the grassroots organizations with the purpose of strengthening their comprehensive health as a fundamental pillar for their work supporting migrants. ---------------------------------------------- 2023: Progress and examples results related to the first objective: Strengthened capacity and advocacy of grassroot migrant organisations:
A main result during 2023 is the completion of the mapping and identification of grass root organizations of migrants interested in participating in the project. This led to a selection of fifteen organizations, five in each of Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador. These organizations consist of returning migrants (most of them deported from the USA), families of non-accompanied migrating minors, labor migrants/seasonal workers, committees of families of missing migrants and people at risk to migrate. The 15 selected grass root migrant organizations are all advancing their processes of organizational strengthening, focusing on communication, advocacy work and monitoring. Most of them have completed their plans for advocacy work to enhance the rights of migrants. The first transfer of funds to the organizations have been made and activities to carry out the advocacy plans are ongoing. As part of the organizational development 43 female leader from the grass root migrant organizations have completed a training program strengthening their leadership qualities. In all three countries the organizations participate in exchanges aiming to strengthen alliances for joint objectives. The civil society platform, RROCM (Red Regional de Organizaciones Civiles para las Migraciones) has elaborated and started to implement a five-year strategic plan where migrant organizations from the region participate to promote their advocacy work at the regional level. Some of the 15 organizations participating in the project have become members of RROCM or are considering joining the network. In December 2023 RROCM was given the opportunity to present its strategic plan and annual plan for 2024 and coordinate activities with the multilateral mechanism the Regional Conference on Migration (CRM). In Honduras 13 organizations met for a first meeting of the national chapter of RROCM.
Progress and examples of results related to the second objective: Design and establish models för three-party cooperation to support local socio-economic integration of migrants.
Three pilot municipalities, or associations of neighboring municipalities, have been selected and activities have been initiated to identify and bring together local authorities, private sector actors and organisations of returning migrants, as well as those considering to migrate, to elaborate a road map for the local integration of migrants or, in some cases strengthen opportunities for people at risk of forced migration. So far there seems to have been more progress related to the commitment of civil society and local authorities elaborating of municipal policies, while mayor results are yet to been seen when it comes to private sector involvement. During the remaining activity period more focus will be on local employment possibilities and the matching of local private sector in need of trained and prepared human capital and the (returning) migrants who need access to income opportunities.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
